findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Two out of the four handwashing sinks in the kitchen area were without hand soap. Discussed with the PIC. New batteries were added to the soap dispenser and soap was provided. Ensure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was mold observed on a couple strawberries stored inside a container within the walk in cooler. Shown to the PIC and the strawberries were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food is always in good condition and never containing mold on surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw chicken was observed above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods and a container of eggs within both the walk in cooler and a prep cooler. Shown to PIC and the chicken products were placed to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. There are many reference sheets for proper storage order posted throughout the kitchen area. Ensure that all chicken products are stored at the bottom shelf to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A red cutting board was observed stored behind handles of the triple sink. Discussed the possibility of contaminating the food contact surface due to improper storage location. Faucet handles aren't typically cleaned frequently as needed to keep them clean, therefore, refrain from storing cutting board behind handles. The board was placed through the dish machine and stored in another location to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Breaded shrimp inside of the 2 door black line cooler (across from cookline) was probed at 57F. The ambient temperature of the cooler was recorded between 57F-61F. All food items were transferred to the walk in cooler since the items were placed inside of the unit at 11am. Violation corrected. Ensure that all TCS foods are cold held at a temperature of 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was a container of breading (used to bread seafood) being stored inside of the dry storage area. The dry breading contained leftover pieces of seafood and is used to bread shrimp and fish for frying purposes. Discussed the need of sifting batter frequently and refrigerating batter if there are plans to reuse the next day. Refrain from storing batters on counters if not refrigerated at end of night. The breading was pulled from shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that batters are sifted at least every few hours and/or held under refrigeration.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The black two door cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F. Both internal thermometers recorded between 57F-61F. The cooler is holding various Time/Temperature Control Foods (TCS) such as seafood and meats. The items were placed inside of the unit at opening time (11am). The facility was instructed to place foods inside of the walk in cooler until the unit can be serviced. Will follow-up August 6, 2026 to see that unit has been repaired or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There is a dispense rack that stores unwrapped ice cream cones in the service area. The ice cream station is self serve, however, the food contact surface is exposed to contamination, as the cone lacks protection. Discussed purchasing wrapped cones with the PIC so that customers aren't able to contamination bare ice cream cones.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There is waste water starting to back up at the drain in front of the cookline. The PIC mentioned contacting a plumber in the past but the company has yet to arrive. Ensure that plumbing is serviced to prevent waste water from back up in floor drain. Will follow-up August 6, 2026 to see that plumbing has been serviced.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility’s temperature sanitizing dish machine appears to not be functioning properly. The machine was cycled at least six times and the surface temperatures ranged between 145F-152F. The PIC will contact a service technician to have the machine repaired. Temperatures for accurately measuring sanitizing levels for food contact surfaces shall be at least 160F. Ensure that the machine is repaired and reaching at least 160F. Will follow-up on 4/27/2026 to make sure that the machine is reaching proper sanitizing temperatures. In the meantime, the facility was instructed to use the triple sink for sanitizing food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There weren’t any sanitizer solutions available in the kitchen area, despite the kitchen being in full operation. Several buckets were prepared and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Discussed with the person-in-charge (PIC) that sanitizer solutions shall always be available if the facility is preparing, handling, and serving food to the public. Ensure that sani solutions are present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: After almost completing the handwashing process, an employee was observed drying his hands with the same paper towel he used to turn off the faucet handles. Educated staff and the employee on proper handwashing to correct the violation. Ensure that a fresh towel is used to dry hands after discarding the hand towel used to operate faucet handles.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was an opened can of ketchup on the top shelf above the preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- An employee switched the ketchup into another container. Educated the employees on transferring highly acid foods to a different can to prevent corrosion after opening, especially if the food item is acidic, such as ketchup or tomato sauce. Ensure that food packages are in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT- The inspectors observed multiple incidents of improper storage order in the facility’s cold holding units:

1. There was a pan of raw shrimp above packages of cooked crawfish in the bottom of a kitchen preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The raw shrimp was placed below the cooked crawfish. 
2. There was a container of marinated raw beef stored above a container of cooked chicken in a standing double-door cooler. CORRECTED- The marinated raw beef was moved to be below the container of cooked chicken. 
3. There was a container of breaded raw fish above a box of ready-to-eat eggrolls in a standing cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The eggrolls were moved to be above the container of breaded raw fish. 
4. There were several containers of raw meats or seafood stored above other raw meats with higher cooking temperatures inside of the walk in cooler. CORRECTED - the containers were rearranged during the visit

Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order. There are multiple storage order handouts posted in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffle of the ice machine in the sushi area was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the outer surface. Discussed with the PIC and the baffle was sanitized to correct the violation. Additionally, the blade of the can opener was observed heavily soiled with dried debris. The can opener was placed through the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that surfaces that come in contact with foods are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizing dispenser at the triple sink wasn't functioning properly. The PIC mentioned that the water isn't pulling through the lines to mix with the quaternary ammonium compound. The facility mostly uses the dish machine to sanitize dishes and bleach is used in their sanitizers buckets, however, the triple sink is sometimes used to sanitize dishes. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired to allow for the water and sanitizer to dispense proportionately. Will follow-up on April 6, 2026 to ensure that the plumbing has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was a container of teriyaki sauce by the hibachi cook-line that was observed to be sitting at room temperature. The label states to “Refrigerate After Opening”. The PIC stated that the bottle was opened yesterday, as they typically go through a bottle a day. The PIC and Kitchen Manager were educated that the teriyaki sauce needs to be refrigerated after opening. CORRECTED- The teriyaki sauce was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are being held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed a container of bean sprouts held on an ice bath to be improperly placed on ice. The bottom of the container was stored on the surface of the ice. The inspector demonstrated  how to properly place containers on ice to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Violation corrected on site. Be sure to educate employees on how to effectively create an ice bath for TCS foods to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
The following items were observed in containers different from its original container:
- Teriyaki sauce stored in a 5 gallon bucket that reads “soy sauce”
- Soy sauce in a bucket that reads “teriyaki sauce”

Discussed with PIC that items that are transferred from its original container must clearly state the food product. Be sure to label food with the correct name.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: One of the double door coolers in the kitchen is observed to have one missing handle that has a string attached to it to allow them to open the door. The other handle on the cooler is observed to be crushed and in disrepair. Ensure that these handles are properly repaired. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
There was observed to be a scoop that was made from the top of a milk gallon bottle. CORRECTED- The scoop was discarded and the staff was educated that food-contact utensils should be durable, able to withstand repeated warewashing, and are smooth and easily cleanable. The staff were educated to use a proper scoop that is intended for use with food. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The shelves of the double-door cooler (also missing handles) are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. This was shown to the PIC, who stated that they will clean the shelves tonight. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hot water available in the men’s bathroom. The PIC mentioned that a knob must’ve been mistakenly switched to stop the flow of hot water. Warm water became available during the inspection. Ensure that hot water is available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The caulking of the handwashing sink in the hibachi and sushi preparation area is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. Ensure that this caulking is re-done and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. There is a gap between the caulking of the handwashing sink by the main cook-line in the kitchen and the wall. Ensure that this caulking is re-done and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The handwashing sink in the dish room and the triple sink is in need of recaulking. The current caulk has pulled away from the wall. Ensure that these sinks are recaulked. 
4. There is tape being used as a repair mechanism on the wall behind the hibachi cold-holding. Ensure that the crack in the wall is properly repaired. Tape is not an approved repair mechanism.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: The facility does not have a designated person in charge (PIC) to exhibit managerial duties such as ensuring that employees are educated on proper food safety and understanding the risks of unsafe food handling practices. The designated PIC should be available to assist inspectors during routine food inspections.The facility has a history of improperly cold holding TCS foods, incorrect storage order, inadequate equipment for temperature control, lacking records for time controlled items, incorrect handwashing, etc. Based on the various priority and priority foundation violations observed during routine visits, SCPDH will continue to issue follow-ups and monitor the progress of the facility’s understanding of food safety. Ensure that there is always a PIC present during operational hours.
findings.citation_text: 2-101.11(A) Assignment. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, the PERMIT HOLDER shall be the PERSON IN CHARGE or shall designate a PERSON IN CHARGE and shall ensure that a PERSON IN CHARGE is present at the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed washing hands without using proper handwashing procedures. The employee was observed rinsing hands without using soap. The activity was ceased and corrected on site. The employee was instructed to wash hands at a different hand-sink using the following steps: rinse hands under warm running water, apply soap and lather hands for at least ten seconds, rinse hands under running water until soap is completely removed, use a single service towel to dry hands, turn faucet handles off with the same paper towel to avoid recontaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a hand washing sink in the kitchen (across from the dish machine) to not have soap. Education was provided to the person in charge regarding stocking all hand washing sinks. CORRECTED- employees were instructed by the PIC to wash hands at one of the other hand washing sinks in the kitchen for the time being. All hand washing must be supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels. Inspector will check that all hand washing sinks are appropriately stocked during 12/01/25 follow up inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper storage order in the facility’s cold holding units:
1) In the walk in cooler there was raw chicken stored over scallops.
2) In a kitchen prep cooler raw chicken was being stored over ready-to-eat (RTE) sauces.
3) In a kitchen prep cooler red meat was being stored above crayfish.
CORRECTED- all items were moved to reflect proper storage order.  Inspectors provided multiple handouts in Mandarin that show correct storage order. Ensure all animal proteins are stored BELOW ready-to-eat (RTE) food items, by increasing internal cooking temperatures- items with higher temperatures should be stored at the bottom of the cooling unit to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) A significant amount of soil debris was observed on the front and back baffles of the facility’s ice machines. Inspector will return on 12/01/25 to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized.
2) The can opener in the kitchen. CORRECTED- item was moved to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of RTE foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Several TCS foods stored on the salad station and the floor dessert case were observed with an internal temperature between 45F-57F. These items included but aren't limited to cut lettuce, tomatoes, dairy based dressing, cheeses, pasta salads, cheesecakes, and other desserts. PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11:00am. PIC also mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is expected to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS items. Foods were discarded voluntarily. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: The facility has a Time as Public Health Control (TAC) policy for the sushi area (rolls and sushi rice). There were no markings or system present to indicate the time the food items were put out during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the time each of the foods under TAC were put out were marked with stickers on the buffet glass. Ensure all TAC items are marked to indicate the time of preparation. Foods held out of temperature for over four hours allow for the growth of harmful pathogens, which may cause foodborne illness.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The hibachi cold line, the salad cold line, and the floor dessert case aren’t maintaining proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods. See violations #22. Foods were probed between 45F-57F. Shown to discussed to PIC and TCS foods were discarded. The facility adds ice to the cold-well to help maintain temperatures. The inspectors observed the ice levels to be extremely low. Employees added more ice to the cold well. Ensure that the unit is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a gap in the bottom right corner of the kitchen back door. Openings between the indoors and outdoors of food establishments may allow for the entry of pests. Replace weather stripping by next routine inspection to close all gaps.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple wet wiping cloths being stored on counters during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- inspector provided education to the PIC. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution in between uses. Moist sanitizer cloths sitting out may allow for the growth and harborage of harmful microorganisms.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The heat puck used to measure the dish machine’s surface temperature was observed without batteries. Discussed with PIC. The facility mentioned purchasing batteries to power the device. Ensure that all temperature measuring devices are available and properly functioning to be sure that dishes are getting sanitized correctly.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple physical facilities in need of repair:
1) The tiles in front of meat walk in cooler.
2) Two hand washing sinks IN the kitchen (near the dish machine and along the cook-line) contain gaps between the sink and wall.
These spaces may allow for the entry of food debris, and moisture. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There were several missing light bulbs inside of the two-door coolers along the cook-line. The coolers are stored across from the fryers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that lighting is available in all cold holding equipment.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: The tongs stored in the cooked rice along the buffet line was observed with the handle touching cooked noodles (directly behind the rice). The handle of the tongs is used by the consumer. Be sure that employees monitor utensils that are being stored on the buffet line to prevent the contamination of other food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-306.13(C) Consumer Self-Service Operations. (C) CONSUMER self-service operations such as buffets and salad bars shall be monitored by FOOD EMPLOYEES trained in safe operating procedures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were at least two containers of raw meats stored about Ready-to-eat food items in the cooler across from the cook-line. The meat containers contained raw beef and raw chicken and the RTE food items were butter and mushrooms. Discussed proper storage order with PIC and items were rearranged. Ensure that all raw animal proteins are stored below RTE foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Several TCS foods stored on the hibachi cold table were observed with an internal temperature between 48F-55F (probed). PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11am. PIC mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is expected to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS items which included cooked rice, crab meat, cooked sausage, and cooked noodles. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Several TCS food items such as but not limited to salad dressings, cut tomatoes, and cut lettuces were probed between 47F-55F along the salad buffet line. PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11am. PIC mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is supposed to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS food items. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less. 

In addition, several containers of cheesecakes stored in the floor dessert case were probed at 63F. The cheesecakes were also discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A bottle of WD-40 was stored above a prep table across from the cookline. Discussed and shown to PIC and bottle was removed. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored in a manner that protects against food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A giant pot of mashed potatoes was observed to be in the process of cooling after being cooked. PIC mentioned that the potatoes had been cooling for no longer than an hour. The facility was instructed to place the pot of mashed potatoes into the walk in cooler and uncover the pot in order to cool properly. The mashed potatoes were probed at 128F. Be sure to use proper cooling methods to ensure that TCS foods are getting cooled properly and reduce the amount of time that food is in the temperature danger zone.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The hibachi cold well isn’t maintaining proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods. See violations #22. Foods were probed between 47F-55F and discarded. A follow-up is scheduled for June 11, 2025 to ensure that the unit is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: At least 3 packages of fish were observed thawing in the original packaging under refrigeration. According to the packaging’s label, reduced oxygen packaged fish must be taken out of the package first before being thawed. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that ROP food is never thawed in its packaging.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Several white powders stored in containers in the dry storage area lacked proper labeling. These items consisted of flour, sugar, and other breading mixes. Ensure that white powders are properly labeled with the name of the food item so that they aren’t mistakenly used.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
There were several acidic foods being stored in their original containers in many areas of the facility including but not limited to dry storages areas and coolers. Due to the acidity of these food products (soy sauce, ketchup, oyster, hoisin, etc), the containers can become damaged if the food sits for long periods of time. Ensure that acidic foods are transferred to a more appropriate container after opening. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: A floor open cooler that stores dessert treats was observed to not have a cover to protect treats from contamination. Discussed with PIC and treats were pulled from floor cooler. The inspector suggested either individually plastic wrapping the desserts or providing clear disposable containers for storage. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Shelled eggs were observed stored above corn on the cob in a prep cooler across from the cookline. Discussed with PIC and items were rearranged. Ensure that eggs are always stored on the bottom shelf to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A sani bucket placed along the sushi line was tested at 0ppm (CL). PIC added more bleach to the solution and was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that sani buckets are at the proper concentration to accurately sanitize surfaces and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility could not locate a temperature measuring device for the dish machine. Discussed with PIC acceptable measuring devices. Ensure that a temperature measuring buffet is available to accurately test dish machine’ sanitizing temperature.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Several mop heads were observed in the basins of mop buckets. Discussed with PIC and mops were placed on hooks. Ensure that mop heads are placed in a position that allows for them to properly air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following places are in need of repairs:
- Missinh floor tiles at entrance of walk in freezer
- Missing wall piece to left of hibachi grill
Ensure that physical facilities are maintained and are always in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a couple tubs of cooked noodles to be stored underneath fly traps that contained dead flies in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC proper food storage and tubs were placed back into the walk in cooler. Ensure that food is stored in a manner the protects against contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Several fly sticky traps were observed above food and food preparation areas in the kitchen. These areas include but aren’t limited to prep tables across from the cook-line and above tubs of cooked noodles. Discussed with PIC that fly traps can’t be placed over food and food preparation areas. The traps were taken down and repositioned to an appropriate location. Ensure that fly traps are stored in a location that will prevent contamination. 

6-202.13: (A) Insect control devices used to stun or electrocute flying insects shall be designed to retain insect in device. (B) Devices shall be installed where it is not located over FOOD preparation area and dead insects and fragments cannot impel or fall into exposed FOOD or FOOD-EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed the back kitchen door to be propped open with a rock. Discussed with PIC and rock was removed. Ensure that kitchen doors are never propped open. This can allow entry for unwanted rodents and insects. Ensure the doors leading to the outside are never propped open. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed several boxes of food to be stored on the floor in the walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC proper food storage. Ensure that food boxes are stored at least 6 inches off the floor or in a manner that protects against contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
A floor display cooler that stores dessert treats was observed to not have a cover to protect treats. Discussed with PIC. The inspector suggested either plastic wrapping the desserts individually or providing clear disposable containers to store the treats. The facility is expecting to provide a cover for the case and the desserts were pulled from the cooler by the owner. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed several stacks of plates along the cook line to be stored with the food contact surface faced upward. Discussed with PIC and plates were turned face down. Ensure that clean plates are stored face down to prevent food contact surfaces from contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
There wasn't any sani buckets present in the kitchen area during food preparation. Discussed with PIC and sani buckets were created. The solution tested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that sani buckets are available whenever food preparation is occurring to properly sanitize surfaces. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.
